cohort: 200 individuals undergoing elective cesarean section randomly assigned to two groups (n=100 each) receiving either a short or long course of antibiotics.
finding: A shorter duration of antibiotic treatment is as effective as a longer duration, with no significant differences observed between the groups in terms of  febrile morbidity, wound induration, serous wound discharge, purulent wound discharge, wound gaping, or atypical vaginal discharge.
